# Siteaccesses and languages of cjw_multisite

A `cjw_multisite` installation has one public site, served in every language you choose, plus the administration.
This page lists the siteaccesses it gets, how their names and settings follow from the languages chosen at install
time, and what to choose for the starter content. It is for administrators planning an install and hosts setting up
addresses; the settings named are written by `cjw-multi-site-installer.php` (see
[The installer scripts](the-installer-scripts.md)).

## The siteaccesses at a glance

With the command from the package description, `--languages=eng-US,ger-DE` and the default primary language
`eng-US`:

| Siteaccess | Serves | Design | Made by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `site` | the starter site in the primary language (`eng-US`) | `starter`, then `standard` | the setup, then `postInstallUserSiteaccessINIUpdate()` |
| `ger` | the starter site in `ger-DE` | the same (a copy of `site`) | `createTranslationSiteAccesses()` |
| `admin` | the administration | `admin4l`, then `admin4`, `admin3`, `admin2`, `admin` | the setup, then `postInstallAdminSiteaccessINIUpdate()` |
| `editor` | the administration for content editing | as made from `admin` | the setup (`eZStepCreateSites::createEditorSiteAccess()`) |
| `adminui` | the administration in the AdminUI design | `adminui` | `postInstallCreateAdminUISiteaccess()`, only when `extension/exp_adminui` is there |

Unlike `sevenx_multisite`, there are no secondary sites: `secondarySiteaccessList()` returns an empty list, and the
step `createSecondarySiteaccesses` only logs "No secondary siteaccesses provided by this installation".

## Choosing the languages

The starter content is mostly German. Of the 137 objects in `cjw-starter-import.json`, 111 exist only in `ger-DE`,
22 only in `eng-US` and 4 in both. So:

| You choose | You get | Starter content |
|---|---|---|
| `eng-US` and `ger-DE` (recommended by the package description) | `site` in English, `ger` in German | complete in `ger`; `site` shows the English objects and, with `ger-DE` in its `SiteLanguageList`, the German ones |
| `ger-DE` as primary, `eng-US` as further language | `site` in German, `eng` in English | complete in `site` |
| `eng-US` alone | `site` only | the kernel adds `ger-DE` as a fallback content language (no siteaccess) so the German objects install |

The last row is what the 6.0.15 changelog describes for `eZStepCreateSites::contentFallbackLanguages()`: before it,
such an install logged 125 errors and the site could not show that content. The installer itself also adds `eng-US`
as a fallback language when the chosen languages lack it (`fallback_locales`).

```bash
# English site plus German translation siteaccess
./console exp:install --package=cjw_multisite --languages=eng-US,ger-DE

# German as the main site, English as the translation
./console exp:install --package=cjw_multisite --language=ger-DE --languages=eng-US
```

`--language` and `--languages` are described in [The console install](../../../install/07-console-install.md); the
kickstarter uses `[language_options] Primary` and `Languages[]` (see [The kickstarter](../../../install/06-kickstarter.md)).

## How a translation siteaccess is named

Every chosen language other than the primary one gets a siteaccess. Its name comes from
`eZSiteInstaller::languageNameFromLocale()` (`kernel/classes/ezsiteinstaller.php`): the part of the locale before the
hyphen, so `ger-DE` gives `ger` and `eng-US` gives `eng`. Then:

- Two chosen locales of one language (`eng-US` and `eng-GB`): the first keeps the short name, later ones add their
  country (`eng_gb`).
- The names `site`, `admin`, `editor`, `adminui` and the chosen user, admin and editor siteaccess names are taken; a
  translation that would collide with one gets its country added, then a number.

## What each public siteaccess is set to

The user siteaccess (`settings/siteaccess/site/`):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `[DesignSettings] SiteDesign`, `AdditionalSiteDesignList[]` | `starter`; `standard` |
| `[SiteAccessSettings] ExtensionSettingsSiteAccess` | `cjw_starter` (the siteaccess settings of `cjw_themes_jumper`) |
| `[SiteAccessSettings] PathPrefix` | the URL alias of the starter root (the object "Starter"; `starter` in the installer's comments) |
| `[SiteSettings] IndexPage`, `DefaultPage` | `/content/view/full/<node of cjw-starter-n-779>`, the start page |
| `[SiteSettings] RootNodeDepth`, content.ini `[NodeSettings] RootNode` | the depth and node id of the starter root |
| `[SiteSettings] SiteName` | the site title, `CJW JAC Exponential` by default |
| `[RegionalSettings] Locale`, `ContentObjectLocale`, `SiteLanguageList` | the primary language; it, the other chosen languages, then the fallback languages |
| `[RegionalSettings] ShowUntranslatedObjects` | `disabled` |
| `[SiteAccessSettings] RequireUserLogin`, `ShowHiddenNodes` | `false`, `false` |

A translation siteaccess is a copy of it with its own `Locale` and `ContentObjectLocale`, `TextTranslation=enabled`
(`disabled` for `eng-GB`), `SiteLanguageList` starting with its own locale, `ShowUntranslatedObjects=enabled`,
`[ContentSettings] TranslationList` set to its locale, and its own `SiteURL`. Its menus are copied from the user
siteaccess after the package node fix (`copySiteaccessMenus()`).

The starter layouts' siteaccess rules name the user siteaccess and all translation siteaccesses
(`cjwSeedStarterLayouts()`), and so do the privacy and cookie policy settings (`postInstallStarterPolicyPages`).

## Addresses and matching

`settings/override/site.ini.append.php` gets:

```ini
[SiteAccessSettings]
AvailableSiteAccessList[]=site
AvailableSiteAccessList[]=ger
# ... admin, editor, adminui
MatchOrder=uri;host
PathPrefixExclude[]=Media
PathPrefixExclude[]=Users
ForceVirtualHost=true

[SiteSettings]
DefaultAccess=site
RootNodeDepth=1
```

`MatchOrder` is `uri;port` when the install uses port access. With URL access the translation is reached by path
(`https://www.example.com/ger/`). With port access a translation gets the next port after the site's; with host access
the installer's comment names the form `ger.example.com`. See
[Siteaccess host and language matching](../../../features/6.0/siteaccess-host-and-language-matching.md).

One session covers all public siteaccesses (`[Session] SessionNamePerSiteAccess=disabled` on the user siteaccess),
while the admin keeps a session of its own (`SessionNameHandler=custom` in the override).

## The language switcher

`[RegionalSettings] TranslationSA` maps each public siteaccess to the name of its language in that language, without
the country: `Deutsch (Deutschland)` becomes `Deutsch` (`translationSALabel()`). It is written to the user siteaccess,
the translations (as copies) and the admin, never to `settings/override`, because a whole-array setting there would
wipe the siteaccesses' own. The starter design's switcher reads it.

## The administration siteaccesses

- `admin`: login required, `ShowHiddenNodes=true`, content root node 2, `Locale` and `SiteLanguageList` from the
  chosen languages, `ActiveAccessExtensions[]` with `expai` and `exp_adminui` where present. See
  [admin4l](../../../features/6.0/admin4l.md).
- `editor`: made by the setup from the admin's files; see
  [The setup wizard and the editor siteaccess](../../../features/6.0/setup-wizard-and-editor-siteaccess.md).
- `adminui`: reached by URI only (`/adminui`), with no host, port or host match entry. See
  [exp_adminui](../../../features/6.0/exp-adminui.md).

> **Note**
> Anonymous may sign in on every served siteaccess except `admin` and `adminui` (`siteRoles()`), so the editor
> siteaccess and the public ones accept the login form.
